skill.name: codex-pet
skill.description: Creates Codex Pet assets from one reference image using RunComfy GPT Image 2 and ImageMagick. The workflow generates a canonical pose, builds the required nine-row spritesheet, writes pet.json, and installs both files into the Codex pets directory.
skill.summary: Builds Codex Pet spritesheets and manifests from one source image.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown examples, but several are confirmed because the skill instructs running RunComfy, ImageMagick, and shell file operations. No prompt-injection attempt was found in SKILL.md. Main residual risks are third-party image processing, local hidden configuration writes, and RunComfy token handling.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running RunComfy, ImageMagick, npm, or package-manager commands.
Validate pet names as safe slugs before using them in RUN_DIR, pet.json, or the Codex install path.
Warn users that the source image URL and prompt are sent to RunComfy before generation starts.
Use scoped RunComfy tokens, document revocation, and keep token files restricted to the current user.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Pet Name Controls File Paths
semantic_findings.description: PET_NAME is used to build the run directory, manifest values, and Codex install path without validation. A name containing path separators or parent directory segments could write outside the intended pet folder.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shell recipe directly interpolates PET_NAME into RUN_DIR, pet.json, and DEST. The variables are quoted, which reduces shell injection risk, but no slug validation prevents path traversal.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Image Processing Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends the source image URL and generation prompt to RunComfy for model processing. Users need an explicit privacy warning before submitting sensitive images or private URLs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The runcomfy command includes the user source image URL in the input JSON, and the privacy section confirms server-side fetching. This is intended behavior but has clear privacy impact.

content.value_statement: Creating a Codex Pet requires a precise spritesheet and manifest. This skill uses RunComfy and ImageMagick to generate and install those assets from one source image.
actual_capabilities: Generates a canonical Codex Pet image through RunComfy GPT Image 2 edit.
Assembles a 1536x1872 spritesheet with nine Codex animation rows.
Converts a magenta chroma-key background into transparent sprite cells.
Writes a pet manifest and installs files in the Codex pets directory.
Provides ImageMagick tuning guidance for subtle animation changes.
Documents prerequisites, exit codes, and privacy considerations.
limitations: Requires RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy token, ImageMagick, and a public source image URL.
Sends the source image URL and generation prompt to RunComfy.
Uses one canonical pose, so animation uses subtle transforms instead of generated frames.
Sample shell commands do not validate custom pet names before creating paths.

use_cases.title: Design a personal Codex companion
use_cases.description: Create a custom desktop pet from a profile image, mascot, or simple character reference.

use_cases.title: Prepare contest-ready pet assets
use_cases.description: Generate the required manifest and spritesheet format for Codex Pet submissions.

use_cases.title: Prototype team mascot variants
use_cases.description: Repeat the workflow with different source images and compare Codex-ready pet styles.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic pet
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Codex Pet named pixel-fox from this source image URL: https://example.com/fox.png. Use the default style and install it.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve key features
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request that names identity details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Make a Codex Pet from this mascot image. Preserve the red scarf, round glasses, and blue hair. Name it refactor-buddy.

prompt_templates.title: Tune the animation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that adjusts motion feel.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Codex Pet and make the idle motion calmer. Keep the jump subtle and make the review row show a small head tilt.

prompt_templates.title: Audit before installation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the Codex Pet assets, verify the spritesheet dimensions, sanitize the pet name, and show the destination path before installing.

output_examples.input: Create a Codex Pet from a dog image URL.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a transparent nine-row spritesheet, a manifest, and an installed pet folder for Codex.

output_examples.input: The generated pet has a magenta halo.
output_examples.output: The response explains chroma-key fuzz settings and suggests a safer background color when the subject uses magenta tones.

output_examples.input: Make the jump animation more visible.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the jump row and recommends a small vertical adjustment that keeps motion readable.

best_practices: Use a centered source image with a clear subject and minimal background clutter.
Use safe lowercase pet names with letters, numbers, and hyphens only.
Review generated files and the destination path before installing into Codex.
anti_patterns: Do not use pet names that contain slashes, parent directory segments, or shell metacharacters.
Do not use private or sensitive image URLs unless RunComfy processing is acceptable.
Do not expect dramatic frame-by-frame motion from the one-pose pipeline.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a Codex Pet manifest and spritesheet that Codex can load as a custom desktop pet.

faq.question: Does it require Codex Pro?
faq.answer: No. It uses RunComfy GPT Image 2 through the RunComfy CLI instead of the Codex image generation tool.

faq.question: What credentials are needed?
faq.answer: It requires a RunComfy login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN environment variable for the external generation call.

faq.question: Where are files installed?
faq.answer: The workflow installs pet.json and spritesheet.webp under the Codex pets directory in the user home configuration path.

faq.question: Can it use non-human subjects?
faq.answer: Yes. Pets, objects, food items, mascots, and simple characters can be converted into the Codex Pet style.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review the source image URL, pet name, RunComfy token handling, and final install path.
